justification: Two config lines and no code: scope an existing cancel-in-progress to pull requests, and stop tracking a per-session hook marker. No product behaviour changes and nothing is served differently.

break_it.scenario: Two merges land on main seconds apart, as #888 and #834 did on 2026-08-11.
break_it.what_happens: Under the old unscoped cancel-in-progress the first merge commit's gates run was cancelled, leaving a commit on main that nothing ever checked — the exact condition main-red-alarm exists to detect. Scoping cancellation to pull_request means main runs always finish and always produce a verdict.
break_it.how: cancel-in-progress is now the expression github.event_name == 'pull_request', so it is false on a push to main. PR force-pushes, which are routine during rebases here, still cancel their superseded runs.

break_it.scenario: A session runs /pre-impl, the marker is rewritten, and the branch is later rebased onto a main where another session did the same.
break_it.what_happens: Before this change .claude/.pre-impl-done.json was tracked, so every such rebase stopped on a conflict in a file that describes a session rather than the codebase. It conflicted on every branch rebased on 2026-08-11. Now it is ignored and untracked, so it cannot conflict.
break_it.how: git rm --cached plus a .gitignore entry. The file stays on disk, so the pre-impl gate that reads it keeps working locally; only git stops tracking it.

break_it.scenario: Someone reads this PR as a fix for the exhausted GitHub Actions allowance.
break_it.what_happens: They stop looking for the real cause and CI stays dead. This changes no run COUNT — concurrency already existed, so superseded runs were already being cancelled. The allowance is exhausted because of run volume and a $0 spending limit with no card on file, which no workflow edit can fix.
break_it.how: Stated in the PR body and in ~/.claude/plans/meta-session-reconciliation-2026-08-11.md: the free fix is a self-hosted runner. This PR is a correctness fix that happens to live in the same file.

break_it.scenario: The Windows machine is asleep or WSL is shut down when someone pushes a PR.
break_it.what_happens: No runner is listening, so every job QUEUES instead of failing. The PR shows checks pending forever, which reads as 'still running' — the same misleading state a conflicting PR produced, and the reason check_pr_gates.py exists.
break_it.how: runs-on reads the repo variable RUNNER_LABEL rather than a literal, so unsetting it returns every job to ubuntu-latest with no code change and no PR. check_pr_gates.py still refuses to merge while no successful run exists for the head sha, so a queued job cannot be mistaken for a pass.

post_merge.db_reset: No. No database access of any kind.
post_merge.secrets: No credentials read or written. Note separately that 4 distinct secrets sit in 17 tracked files; that is not addressed here and needs rotation.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes. After the next two merges to main land close together, confirm both merge commits have a completed gates run rather than a cancelled one.
